title: SHM Acceleration
prompt:
A particle in simple harmonic motion has displacement x(t) = 2*cos(3*t).

Find its acceleration a(t) = d²x/dt².
recap:
Simple harmonic motion is x(t) = A·cos(ω t): a restoring force proportional to displacement. Differentiate once for velocity v = −A·ω·sin(ω t), again for acceleration a = −A·ω²·cos(ω t) = −ω²·x — always toward equilibrium, with magnitude set by ω².

Example — x(t) = 3·cos(2t): v = −6·sin(2t), a = −12·cos(2t) (= −4·x, since ω² = 4).

The defining relation a = −ω²·x is what makes the motion sinusoidal with angular frequency ω. Reference: Kleppner & Kolenkow, An Introduction to Mechanics, ch. 11.
